function: Channel estimation for multiuser MIMO-OFDM: a conditional GAN refines least-squares channel estimates into accurate channel matrices (p. 2-4).
system: Multiuser MIMO-OFDM, N=4 single-antenna users, BS with M=32 antennas, K=32 subcarriers; no RIS; frequency band not stated (p. 3, 9).
method: Conditional GAN (U-Net generator, patch discriminator) trained offline, supervised and adversarial, on paired LS-estimate/true-channel samples, plus self-preserving and cycle-consistency losses (p. 4-8).
data_channel: Simulated SCM channel model [45], [46], urban micro and urban macro scenarios; 40000 samples each, split 24000 train, 12000 test, 4000 validation (p. 7, 9).
test_conditions: Trained in urban micro; tested in urban micro plus urban macro, with delay spread from 6 to 11, and with pilot contamination (p. 11-13).
baselines: Classical: LMMSE, RLMMSE. Learned: MLP, SF-CNN [18], original cGAN [36], plus own baseline cGAN and ablation models A-E (p. 9-11).
metrics: NMSE versus SNR (-5 to 15 dB); NMSE over training epochs; FLOPs order of magnitude (p. 9, 11).
complexity: Order of FLOPs: improved cGAN about 10^7 versus SF-CNN about 10^8; formulas for LMMSE O((MK)^3), RLMMSE O(MK log K), cGAN layer sum (p. 9).
openness: none (no code or data link stated; implementation only names Python 3.7.13 and tensorflow 2.0.0, p. 9).
q1_support: p. 7: "We use the SCM channel model [45], [46] to generate channel samples"; p. 14: "Extending the 3GPP spatial channel model (SCM)" (title of ref. [45]). Standardized 3GPP SCM, not TR 38.901; see notes.
q2_support: p. 12: "We first train the cGAN models in the urban micro scenario. Then, we test the trained cGAN models in both the urban micro scenario and the urban macro scenario."
q3_support: p. 9: "the DL-based schemes (MLP, SF-CNN [18], and the original cGAN proposed in [36]), and conventional channel estimation approaches (e.g., LMMSE and RLMMSE)"; p. 11: "the improved cGAN model achieves the best NMSE performance among all methods"
q4_support: p. 9: "The complexity of the improved cGAN-based method is in the order of magnitude of 107" (printed as 10^7 FLOPs; SF-CNN 10^8, same page).
q5_support: p. 7: "We use the SCM channel model [45], [46] to generate channel samples"; p. 9: "implemented in Python 3.7.13 with tensorflow 2.0.0". Missing: any code or data link or DOI; the channels are self-generated, not a public dataset.
notes: q1 is marked 1 under the rule for another standardized model, for the reviewer to confirm: the paper says only 'SCM channel model [45], [46]' (p. 7) and refs [45], [46] (p. 14) name the 3GPP spatial channel model (SCM, TR 25.996), not TR 38.901; urban micro and urban macro are its scenarios. The text of p. 9 cites the original cGAN as [36] while the Fig. 5 legend (p. 11) says [37]. A RIS appears only in related work (p. 2), not in the system. Pages count the 15 pages of the file.
